title: The Best Are Always the Best: COVID-19 Lockdown Stringency and the Dispersion of Olympic Medal Outcomes
abstract: arXiv:2608.16325v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We ask whether COVID-19 lockdown stringency altered national Olympic performance between Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2020, using the Oxford Stringency Index and the 99 countries that won a medal in either edition. As in \citet{liu2024}, mean performance is unaffected: stringency is insignificant in every OLS and ANOVA specification. The distribution is not. Among the 84 non-traditionally dominant nations, medal changes are three to six times more dispersed in high-stringency countries; the difference is absent among dominant nations and concentrated in men's events. A common shock left the competitive hierarchy intact while sharply raising outcome uncertainty for smaller Olympic teams.

translated_title: 最好的始终是最好的：COVID-19封锁严格性与奥运奖牌结果的离散度
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.16325v1 公告类型：新 摘要：我们利用牛津严格性指数以及在2016年里约和2020年东京奥运会上获得奖牌的99个国家，探讨了COVID-19封锁严格性是否改变了国家奥运表现。正如\citet{liu2024}所述，平均表现未受影响：在所有OLS和ANOVA规格中，严格性均不显著。但分布并非如此。在84个非传统主导国家中，高严格性国家的奖牌变化离散度是其他国家的三到六倍；这种差异在主导国家中不存在，且集中在男子项目中。一个共同冲击保持了竞争等级结构的完整，同时显著提高了较小奥运代表队的结果不确定性。
tldr: 本文发现COVID-19封锁严格性不改变奥运奖牌平均表现，但显著增加了非主导国家，尤其是男子项目中的奖牌结果离散度，而主导国家不受影响。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that COVID-19 lockdown stringency does not alter average Olympic medal performance but significantly increases the dispersion of medal outcomes among non-dominant countries, especially in men's events, while dominant nations remain unaffected.
